blocks.title: 1. Core Concepts
blocks.text:
1. Biological classification

  • Grouping  of the Organisms on the basis of similarities and dissimilarities is called biological classification
Hence, classification systems for living organisms have undergone several changes over time, but the positions of Plantae and animals remain constant.

2. Carolus Linnaeus (Two Kingdom Classification):

In two kingdom classification, prokaryotes and eukaryotes, unicellular and multicellular, autotrophs and heterotrophs, and chitinous walled and cellulosic walled organisms are in the same kingdom.

3. Five kingdom system of classification:-

  • In the five kingdom classification, viruses, viroids, prions and lichens are not mentioned.
  • In five kingdom classifications. Chlamydomonas and chlorella are placed in the kingdom Protista.

  • All prokaryotes like bacteria, cyanobacteria, archaebacteria, mycoplasma, etc are placed under kingdom monera
  • Bacteria are the sole members of the kingdom Monera.

blocks.title: Question:1
blocks.question:
Which one of the following is not an inclusion body found in prokaryotes?

(1) Cyanophycean granule

(2) Glycogen granule

(3) Polysome

(4) Phosphate granule
blocks.answer:
Ans.-3

A polysome is not an inclusion body in prokaryotes. It refers to a cluster of ribosomes that are translating the same mRNA simultaneously, which is a process related to protein synthesis, not a stored substance or inclusion.
blocks.prompt: Which one of the following is not an inclusion body found in prokaryotes?

blocks.title: Question: 2
blocks.question:
The guts of cow and buffalo possess:

(1) Chlorella spp.

(2) Methanogens

(3) Cyanobacteria

(4) Fucus spp.
blocks.answer:
Ans.-2

The guts of cows, buffaloes, and other ruminants harbor methanogens, which are a type of archaea. These microorganisms help in the digestion of plant material by breaking down cellulose in the stomach, and they produce methane as a byproduct of this process. Methanogens thrive in the anaerobic (low oxygen) environment of the rumen and are an essential part of the digestive process in these animals.

blocks.title: 4. Special points: Kingdom Protista
blocks.text:
3. Special points:

  • Diatoms float passively on the surface of water (Plankton) due to low molecular weight stored fats.
  • Dinoflagellates are responsible for Bioluminescence
  • Euglenoids have pigments similar to higher plants.
  • Diatoms are also known as pearls of oceans. e.g. Navicula
  • Dinoflagellates  lacks of histone protein .

blocks.title: Question 1
blocks.question:
Kingdom Protista includes organisms like:

(1) Amoeba, Euglena and Diatoms

(2) Amoeba, Euglena and Penicillium

(3) Amoeba, Spirogyra and Penicillium

(4) Euglena, Spirogyra and Albugo
blocks.answer:
Ans.- 1

Kingdom Protista includes a diverse group of organisms, primarily unicellular eukaryotes. Some examples are:

  • Amoeba (a protozoan) – A unicellular organism that moves and feeds by pseudopodia.
  • Euglena (a flagellate) – A single-celled organism that has both plant-like (photosynthesis) and animal-like (movement using flagella) characteristics.
  • Diatoms (a type of algae) – Single-celled algae that have a silica-based cell wall.

blocks.title: Kingdom:- Fungi
blocks.text:
• The fungi or mycota is a unique kingdom of heterotrophic organisms.
  • They can be seen in from of moulds on bread, butter, leather, pickle, rotten fruits (orange rotting) and vegetables or as parasites in plants (white spot on mustard leaves) and animals.

blocks.title: Question-1
blocks.question:
The imperfect fungi which are decomposers

of litter and help in mineral cycling belong to:

(1) Ascomycetes (2) Deuteromycetes

(3) Basidiomycetes (4) Phycomycetes
blocks.answer:
Ans.-2

Deuteromycetes, also known as "imperfect fungi," are a group of fungi in which the sexual stage of reproduction is either absent or not observed. These fungi are significant decomposers of litter, breaking down organic matter in the soil. This activity contributes to mineral cycling by releasing essential nutrients back into the ecosystem.

blocks.title: Lichen
blocks.text:
• Lichen is composed of algae and fungi or Lichen is a composite thalloid structure of algae and fungi.
  • Lichens are found at those places where normal plants do not grow such as on rocks, cold Arctic regions, on walls etc. Lichens are also found on dead and decaying wooden pieces, leaves, and soil.
Lichen: Algae & Fungi mutualism

Algae: Phycobiont (Provide food)

Fungi: Mycobiont (Provide shelter and absorption of water and minerals)

Lichen are used as pollution indicator, they do not grow in polluted environment

blocks.title: Question:1
blocks.question:
Q.1 Which of the following plant virus has  coiled RNA strand and capsomeres?

(1) Polio virus

(2) Tobacco mosaic virus

(3) Measles virus

(4) Retrovirus
blocks.answer:
Ans.-2

Tobacco mosaic virus (TMV) is characterized by a coiled RNA strand enclosed within a protein coat made of capsomeres. The RNA is single-stranded, and the capsomeres are arranged helically, forming a rigid, rod-shaped structure.
blocks.prompt: Q.1 Which of the following plant virus has  coiled RNA strand and capsomeres?

blocks.title: Question: 2
blocks.question:
Q.2 Viruses have :-

(1) DNA enclosed in a protein coat

(2) Prokaryotic nucleus

(3) Single chromosome

(4) Both DNA and RNA
blocks.answer:
Ans.-1

Viruses are acellular entities that contain either DNA or RNA, but not both. Their genetic material (DNA or RNA) is enclosed within a protein coat called a capsid, which protects the genetic material and helps the virus attach to host cells.
options: (1) DNA enclosed in a protein coat

blocks.title: Question:3
blocks.question:
Q.3 Viroids differ from viruses in having;

(1) DNA molecules without protein coat

(2) RNA molecules with protein coat

(3) RNA molecules without protein coat

(4) DNA molecules with protein coat
blocks.answer:
Ans.-3

Viroids are the simplest infectious agents composed of a short, circular, single-stranded RNA molecule without a protein coat. They lack the capsid that viruses have, and they are known to cause diseases in plants by interfering with their gene expression.

blocks.title: Question: 4
blocks.question:
Q.4 Which of the following statements is incorrect ?

(1) Viroids lack a protein coat

(2) Viruses are obligate parasites

(3) Infective constituent in viruses is the protein coat

(4) Prions consist of abnormally folded Proteins.
blocks.answer:
Ans.-3

Correct statement (1): Viroids lack a protein coat. This is true; viroids are composed solely of RNA molecules without any protective protein coat.

Correct statement (2): Viruses are obligate parasites. This is true; viruses cannot replicate outside a host and rely on host cells for reproduction.

Incorrect statement (3): The infective constituent in viruses is not the protein coat. The infective part of a virus is its genetic material (either DNA or RNA), which carries the information needed to hijack the host cell's machinery. The protein coat (capsid) protects the genetic material and aids in attachment to host cells but is not infective on its own.

Correct statement (4): Prions consist of abnormally folded proteins. This is true; prions are infectious agents made entirely of misfolded proteins, causing diseases like mad cow disease (BSE) and Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease.
options: (3) Infective constituent in viruses is the protein coat
(4) Prions consist of abnormally folded Proteins.
